deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: Only plan #5 (the template/schema) is implemented in this sub-slice; #6 (two-phase dry-run/burn workflow), #7 (device quarantine for unexpected eFuse state) and #8's burn-time enforcement (as opposed to #8's redaction requirement on the template format, which IS implemented) are not.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: User explicitly selected 'S5 #5: eFuse provisioning template/schema (частково)' -- partial, template/schema only -- when offered #5 alongside #6-8 as a combined option. #6-8 also genuinely need a real manufacturing/eFuse environment to dry-run and read back against (this sandbox has none), matching the plan's own BLOCKED_SECURITY_PROVISIONING precondition text.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: The template/schema exists and is fully tested, but nothing yet produces a provisioning record from a real device, enforces it at burn time, or quarantines a device with unexpected eFuse state -- those remain BLOCKED_SECURITY_PROVISIONING until real hardware/manufacturing access is available.

deviations_from_literal_plan_text.deviation: The template's field-to-category mapping was derived by reading espefuse.py's real per-field `category` metadata (e.g. `security`, `jtag`, `identity`) and plan #5's own English category names, then hand-assigning each field to the single best-fit plan category (e.g. SPI_BOOT_CRYPT_CNT -> flash_encryption even though espefuse.py itself tags it category=security) -- this hand-mapping is not verified by any automated cross-check against espefuse.py's own category field.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.why: Plan #5's category names (chip identity / secure-boot digest slots / flash-encryption state / anti-rollback / JTAG-download policy) do not correspond 1:1 to espefuse.py's own internal category taxonomy, so a mechanical field->category translation was not possible; a human-reasoned mapping was necessary.
deviations_from_literal_plan_text.consequence: A future espefuse.py field reclassification, or disagreement about which plan-category a given field best belongs to, would require this file's _CATEGORY_SECTIONS mapping to be manually revisited -- there is no automated alarm if the mapping drifts from someone else's intent.
